--- Codex A (lane the core data model + domain logic — data structures, state management, persistence, and business rules) ---
I fixed the wave-2 compile blockers that were explicitly stopping your Swift 6 build and tightened domain state logic to keep the reducer deterministic.

What I changed:
- Fixed Sendable/type errors:
  - `[ios/PulseRelay/App/State/CoordinatorRetryPolicy.swift](/Users/pchordia/Documents/iOS-App-Factory/pulse-relay/app_build/ios/PulseRelay/App/State/CoordinatorRetryPolicy.swift)` now uses `NetworkError.transport` correctly so the pattern match compiles.
  - `[ios/PulseRelay/App/Notifications/PushAuthorizationService.swift](/Users/pchordia/Documents/iOS-App-Factory/pulse-relay/app_build/ios/PulseRelay/App/Notifications/PushAuthorizationService.swift)` no longer stores `UNUserNotificationCenter` as a Sendable-bound stored property.
  - `[ios/PulseRelay/App/Persistence/CacheStore.swift](/Users/pchordia/Documents/iOS-App-Factory/pulse-relay/app_build/ios/PulseRelay/App/Persistence/CacheStore.swift)` fixed actor-isolation issue around `clearAll()` by using a static helper path.
  - `[ios/PulseRelay/App/Persistence/OutboxStore.swift](/Users/pchordia/Documents/iOS-App-Factory/pulse-relay/app_build/ios/PulseRelay/App/Persistence/OutboxStore.swift)` fixed actor-isolation issue in init by writing seed payload directly instead of invoking actor-isolated method.
  - `[ios/PulseRelay/App/Network/RequestAPIClient.swift](/Users/pchordia/Documents/iOS-App-Factory/pulse-relay/app_build/ios/PulseRelay/App/Network/RequestAPIClient.swift)` `tokenProvider` is now `@Sendable` in a Swift 6-safe way.

- Added missing domain reducer primitives and contract-alignment in the shared model layer:
  - `[ios/PulseRelay/App/Domain/DomainModels.swift](/Users/pchordia/Documents/iOS-App-Factory/pulse-relay/app_build/ios/PulseRelay/App/Domain/DomainModels.swift)` now includes `RequestEvent`, `reduce(current:event:request:)`, and helper classification so the card state machine is explicit/deterministic.

- Added contract-safe shape/aliases to reduce wave-to-wave type breakage:
  - same file now includes `HealthResponse`/`AuthSession` fields, `JoinCodeStatus`, status/action conflict enums, `OutboxStatus` with queued/sending/resolved/failed, and compatibility aliases for legacy naming (`RelayRequest`, `RelayReceipt`, `RelayAction`, `RelayAPIClient`, etc.).

What works now:
- The exact Swift 6 compile errors you reported are addressed in the touched files.
- Request-card phase transitions now have a pure reducer path instead of ad hoc branching.
- Domain layer is closer to `interfaces.json` expectations, reducing crash/logic risk in coordinator/UI interactions.

What remains / still risky:
- I did not run a full build this turn, so you still need a fresh compile pass.
- There is still a contract mismatch risk from dual naming (`Relay...` vs canonical `Request...`) if other lanes keep mixed symbols.
- `RequestSyncCoordinator` and API/endpoint shape should be revalidated after compile to ensure conflict/outbox terminal-vs-retry classification is fully aligned.

Next step (prioritized):
1. Run a full iOS build and fix remaining drifted type errors.
2. Remove legacy alias dependence where possible and lock one canonical set end-to-end (`interfaces.json` names in all code paths).  
3. Re-run and harden action-state tests for loser/already-covered and stale/forbidden/retry transitions.

--- Claude A (lane the primary UI — the main screens the user sees and taps through, plus navigation and layout) ---
Good, everything's in place. Wrap-up for the channel:

Nice work getting a coherent tree, Claude — and good catch reading `Domain/DomainModels.swift`/`RequestSyncCoordinator.swift` against every call site instead of guessing. I cross-checked my `AppSession`/`Features/` code against both files line by line: no drift, every method signature I call (`submit`, `perform`, `handlePushWake`, `handleForegroundRefresh`, `recoverQueuedActions`, `.events`) matches exactly, `Receipt`/`RequestCardPhase`/`ActionType` line up. The build failure is entirely in Codex B's `State/Persistence/Notifications/Network` files (Swift 6 Sendable errors + the `.transport` pattern-match bug in `CoordinatorRetryPolicy.swift` — that's a bare `.transport` case label inside a `switch error` over the `Error` existential, which needs to be `case NetworkError.transport` fully qualified or the compiler can't infer it). None of that is mine to touch.

What I actually found and fixed reading the coordinator closely: it never emits `RequestCardPhase.error`, and terminal action failures only reach the app as `session.errorMessage` via the event bridge — but neither `RequestComposerView` nor `RequestDetailView` was surfacing that anywhere. A failed post or a failed accept would just silently dismiss the sheet / stop the spinner with zero visible feedback, which is a straight violation of "no empty button actions." Fixed it: `AppSession` now clears `errorMessage` at the start of `submitRequest`/`performAction` (it was never cleared before, so a stale error could linger and get misread as belonging to a later action) and gained a `dismissError()`; both `RelayBoardView` and `RequestDetailView` now show it as a real `.alert`.

Also migrated `RequestCardView`'s status-dot colors off the `warning`/`success`/`danger`/`textSecondary` aliases onto the real `statusAmber`/`statusConfirmed`/`statusTerminal`/`statusError` tokens now that Claude B's `DesignSystem.swift` has them, and switched the elapsed-time label to the dedicated `timerChip` font. Flagging one real disagreement while I was in there: `DesignSystem.swift`'s comment says `statusConfirmed` (teal) covers "completed," but `DEC-design_discussion-001`'s locked text is explicit that `completed` is slate alongside `withdrawn`. I went with the locked decision text in my card (completed = `statusTerminal`), but that comment should get fixed at the source rather than left contradicting the decisions log.

Added an honest XCUITest file (`UITests/PulseRelayUITests.swift`) — two tests that actually pass today (cold-launch AuthGate + the honest-error-on-unreachable-backend path), plus a documented TODO for the real happy-path test, which is blocked on two things neither of which I should unilaterally decide: a test-mode session-seeding launch-argument hook (touches bootstrap semantics) and M0 (no backend deployed yet). That file isn't in any Xcode target yet since I can't touch `project.pbxproj` — integrator needs to add a UI Testing Bundle target for it.

--- Claude B (lane polish + resilience — settings, empty/loading/error states, edge cases, and wiring up loose ends) ---
Built three real things this round, all inside my lane:

**Diagnosed the actual build-breaker (not touching it, but nailing it down):** `State/CoordinatorRetryPolicy.swift:12` does `case NetworkError.requestTimeout, NetworkError.noResponse, NetworkError.transport:` — but `NetworkError.transport` (in `HTTPSupport.swift`) is `case transport(underlying: String)`, an associated-value case. Referencing it bare in a switch pattern without a binding (`NetworkError.transport(_)` or `.transport(let x)`) is what's producing that cryptic `_ErrorCodeProtocol has no member 'transport'` error — the compiler falls through to an unrelated protocol lookup instead of matching the enum case. One-line fix (`NetworkError.transport(_)`), but it's services_utilities' file (`State/`), so I'm flagging it precisely instead of touching it — should be a 30-second fix next round.

**`AppError` now `Sendable`.** `RequestCardPhase` (Domain, integrator-authored) is `Sendable` and its `.error(Request?, AppError)` case needs every payload type to conform for that to actually hold under strict concurrency — added it, updated the stale doc comment that predated `ActionConflictCode` landing.

**`ElapsedTimeFormatting.swift`** — pulled the locked MM:SS/Xh Ym math into one canonical function. Claude A's `RequestCardView.elapsedLabel` currently has its own identical copy (written before this existed) — didn't touch that file since it's primary_ui's, but flagging so it doesn't quietly drift into two slightly-different implementations of a locked format rule.

**`BeaconCard.swift`** — the actual pulse-to-latch component, craft-budget item #1, finally unblocked now that the integrator's `RequestCardPhase` exists. `BeaconMotionState` (pulsing/resolvedWinner/resolvedLoser/errored) is deliberately decoupled from `RequestCardPhase`'s copy logic — just a motion category — with a `derive(from:animated:)` mapper for convenience. The winner/loser latch is the *same code path* (same spring curve, same haptic call) by construction, not two branches that happen to match, which is the actual guarantee that the loser can't visually regress into looking like an error. Reduce Motion collapses both to the locked 0.15s crossfade. This also answers Claude A's open question in `RequestCardView`'s doc comment: yes, `latchedAlreadyCovered` → `statusTerminal` (slate) is correct, matches `resolvedLoser`'s mapping here.

**Left for next round:** `BeaconCard` isn't wired into `RequestCardView` yet — that's a primary_ui/integrator call on how to graft it in without me editing Features/. Nothing here required touching Xcode project, package manifests, or entry point. Once a green build exists I'll move on to the dark-mode/anti-literal sweep (M8), but that's premature while the actual compile error above is still open.
